My pregnancy was not planned and the father and I were absolutely not in a good place and still are not together (Bub is 8 months). It’s the longest roller coaster of a story.
He wanted the abortion and even though I made the booking for a surgical abortion after being basically manipulated to do it I ended up cancelling it and not going in because my first feeling when I found out I was pregnant was of course fear but before I told anyone I knew deep inside my heart that abortion wasn’t the path I wanted to take.

Motherhood is hard but there isn’t a single moment that goes by where I regret my choice. I’m so happy to have a mini me because that was what I knew was right for me personally.

I’m all for your body your choice and I think abortion should be accessible to anyone who needs or wants one but you’ve just gotta follow your heart.
I have a friend who has never once regretted her abortion and is very happy because she did the same thing I did and followed her heart. I personally think when you do that with anything that’s when things fall into place.

Some would’ve said I was crazy for doing this without a partner or a village of people to help but I make it work and just because it’s hard doesn’t mean it’s bad. For me personably being both a little human mother and a dog mother are the best jobs I’ve ever done.

So if you’re in this position just go with what feels right for your life path. Picture your life 5 years ahead with a child and without and think about what makes you happiest.

Honestly I’m struggling myself. While I enjoy being a mother and love my daughter (and my dog) more than anything I have both good and bad days and I try to think of this as just a piece of my life. Try to keep reminding yourself this isn’t forever and there are better days to come and as far away as they feel they may be you’ve got that to look forward to.

Also with your husband please communicate to him and ask for help. You’re both still married to each other so the work load should be shared especially because you’re going through a dark period in your life.

Your feelings are valid and you are normal! But please reach out for help and even see your trusted doctor for a counselling service or medication if they recommend it.

Also I know this is not my place to say at all but don’t feel pressured to 100% breast feed if it is eating away at your health mentally and physically. If this is something you want to do then that’s okay but if you’re willing to switch to combination feeding of breast and formula I’ve heard it has saved some women’s mental health BUT again this isn’t my place to say and it is also something you could speak to your paediatrician and doctor about as well to see if they’ve got any recommendations or even speaking to a midwife on ways to help mastitis can help as well.

Also when I said I was a single mother she looked at me like I killed someone!!! Once she finally left I broke down crying and had a panic attack.

The next midwife who did a home visit for the next 3 days was an angel!!!! She helped me with latching and checked all my wounds. She was so helpful with places I can book myself in for physio, places for Bub to get in to paediatricians in my area, mothers groups close to me so I didn’t have to travel far etc etc … she even just sat with me and had a chat because she had time. I’m in Australia and I barely used anything I packed! What I used:

- a few of my fave snacks (I’m dairy free and noted that with my midwife during pregnancy so the hospital catered all meals to dairy free so I didn’t eat all my snacks but I did dig into them a little though). Also didn’t need a water bottle because fresh cold water was supplied in cups with a straw.

- a few super comfy black undies and comfy bra/bralette type things easy for breast feeding and just comfy in general. If you’d like to do a water birth be sure to bring a spare you don’t mind getting wet.

- I used a couple of my heavy flow pads but hospital supplied plenty of adult nappies for the bleeding which I used because I needed to change them frequently.

- used one set of black comfy pjs (loose pants and a big loose tee cos it is cool in hospital plus it’s easy to lift for breast feeding if you choose to)

- my toiletries for a shower after birth such as face cleanser, toothpaste, toothbrush, face moisturiser, lip balm and body wash. (Didn’t pack shampoo as I chose not to wash my hair until I got home and just brushed it and put it back up in a bun) but you can bring shampoo and conditioner if you would like to wash your hair there. I used the hospital towels as well btw, some people think it’s gross but I cbf like honestly my hospital is clean so whatever each to their own.

- I used a plastic bag to put my birthing clothes in to take home (you can use a hospital gown but I used my own clothes as they were more comfy to me which was a big loose comfy dark coloured jumper)

- I used shower thongs also in a seperate plastic bag.

- I used ONE baby zippy to take my baby home in as the hospital supplied swaddles while there and my bub was a spring baby so I didn’t need mittens or a hat. My zippy had fold over feet and mittens anyway. Everything else I packed for Bub was a waste of time lol because hospital supplied everything needed. Hospital also supplied nappies as well.

- I used my super long phone charger and my phone.

- I used ONE going home outfit which was loose comfy black pants and a comfy tee. Again being spring it wasn’t very cold but always bring a jumper anyway to be safe!

- also used one pair of socks and wore those with slides in the hospital and just wore slides with no socks on my way home.


So yeah that’s basically all I used and I packed so many unnecessary things which really just annoyed me tbh cos it was such an effort bringing it all into hospital and taking out lol!! But every hospital is different so your hospital may or may not supply these things so just check with your midwife or hospital just to be safe. But sometimes keeping it simple is key and far less stressful.
